newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI to use open market operations-paper.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI to use open market operations-paper.

text.p: Open market operations will in future be used in conjunction with changes in the bank rate to manage liquidity more effectively, India's central bank chief was quoted as saying by a newspaper on Friday.
"Changes in the bank rate will have to be accompanied by other back-up actions," Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told The Economic Times in an interview.
A mere announcement that the bank rate has changed towards an objective by itself will not do much, he said.

The RBI on Wednesday cut its key bank rate by one percentage point to 10 percent per annum and also announced 100 basis point cuts in deposits with maturities from 30 days to one year and on rupee post-shipment export credit.
Dealers say banks are expected to cut deposit and lending rates in coming days after their individual boards of directors approve the revision in rates.

In a separate interview to the Financial Express, Rangarajan said that domestic borrowings will now be more attractive (after the rate cut) and there could be a shift away from foreign borrowings by Indian corporates.
"With the decline in domestic interest rates, the attraction (for external commercial borrowings) goes down," Rangarajan was quoted as saying in the Financial Express.
"In fact there can be a shift towards borrowing domestically than borrowing externally when the rate comes down," he said.
"If one takes into account the cost of external borrowing - if the expected change in exchange rate is also added - I do not think it will be more attractive than what it is now," Rangarajan said.
